title: Walk it
q: Countries that share a land border with France
rule: Overseas territories count, so the borders of French Guiana and Saint Martin are in.
fact: France's longest land border is with Brazil, via French Guiana. It also touches the Netherlands, on the Caribbean island of Saint Martin.

traps.United Kingdom: The Channel Tunnel isn't a land border.
traps.Austria: Switzerland and Germany sit in between.
traps.Guyana: Suriname sits between Guyana and French Guiana.
traps.Liechtenstein: Switzerland and Austria sit in between.

title: Zed or zee
q: Countries with the letter Z in their name
rule: UN member states, judged on today's English name, so former names don't count.
fact: Herzegovina comes from the German Herzog, 'duke', so Bosnia and Herzegovina is quite literally 'Bosnia and the Duke's land'.

traps.Swaziland: It became Eswatini in 2018, and the Z went with it.
traps.Zanzibar: It's part of Tanzania, not a country.
traps.Zaire: That was the old name of DR Congo, which has no Z today.
traps.Mexico: That's an X, not a Z.

title: Twin initials
q: Capital cities that start with the same letter as their country
rule: UN member states plus the Pope's own state. Any official capital counts, including a country's second capital.
fact: Sri Lanka's parliament sits in Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, a suburb of Colombo, which makes the island an S-for-S match that few people spot.

traps.San Salvador: The country is El Salvador, which starts with E.
traps.Santo Domingo: The country is the Dominican Republic, which starts with D.
traps.Colombo: Colombo starts with C, but Sri Lanka starts with S.
traps.Tripoli: It's Libya's capital, and Libya starts with L.

title: Stan by me
q: Countries whose names end in -stan or -land
rule: Sovereign states only, and the name must end exactly in -stan or -land.
fact: The ending -stan is Persian for 'land', so the seven -stan countries are, in effect, -land countries too.

traps.Netherlands: It ends in -lands, with an S, so it misses by a letter.
traps.Scotland: It's part of the United Kingdom, not a sovereign state.
traps.England: It's part of the United Kingdom, not a sovereign state.
traps.Greenland: It's a self-governing territory of Denmark.

title: Double trouble
q: US states with a double letter in their name
rule: Two identical letters side by side, anywhere in the name. Washington DC isn't a state.
fact: Mississippi and Tennessee are the only states that double up three times: ss-ss-pp and nn-ss-ee.

traps.Alabama: Its four As are never side by side.
traps.Kansas: The two Ss are separated by an A.
traps.Louisiana: No letter doubles up next to itself.
traps.Wisconsin: Two Ss and two Ns, but none side by side.

title: Big neighbourhood
q: Countries that share a land border with China
rule: Mainland land borders only; disputed or undemarcated frontiers still count.
fact: China and Russia share the world record of 14 land neighbours. China meets Afghanistan only at the far end of the narrow Wakhan Corridor.

traps.Thailand: Myanmar and Laos sit in between.
traps.South Korea: Only the Yellow Sea lies between them.
traps.Uzbekistan: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan sit in between.
traps.Bangladesh: India and Myanmar sit in between.
traps.Japan: It's an island nation with no land borders at all.

title: Going with the flow
q: Countries the River Danube flows through or runs along
rule: The Danube itself must pass through the country or form part of its border. Tributaries don't count.
fact: The Danube touches ten countries, more than any other river, but Moldova gets only a short riverfront near Giurgiulești, under a kilometre.

traps.Czechia: It sits in the Danube basin, but the river itself never touches it.
traps.Switzerland: The Inn rises there and joins the Danube later, but the Danube never enters Switzerland.
traps.Slovenia: The Sava drains it into the Danube, but the Danube doesn't touch it.
traps.Bosnia and Herzegovina: The Sava forms its northern border, not the Danube.

title: Zero degrees
q: Countries the Prime Meridian passes through on land
rule: The Greenwich meridian (0 degrees longitude) crossing a country's land. Antarctic claims don't count.
fact: Null Island, where the Prime Meridian meets the Equator at 0°N 0°E, is open sea in the Gulf of Guinea, hundreds of kilometres south of Ghana.

traps.Portugal: All of it lies west of the line.
traps.Ireland: All of it lies west of the line.
traps.Morocco: All of it lies west of the line, which passes through neighbouring Algeria instead.
traps.Benin: All of it lies east of the line.
traps.Netherlands: All of it lies east of the line.

title: Wrong side?
q: Countries where traffic drives on the left
rule: UN member states only, so the four home nations count together as one country.
fact: Samoa switched from the right to the left in 2009, so it could import cheaper right-hand-drive cars from Australia, New Zealand and Japan.

traps.Hong Kong: Traffic keeps left there, but it isn't a country.
traps.Sweden: It switched to driving on the right in 1967.
traps.Nigeria: It switched to driving on the right in 1972.
traps.Myanmar: It switched to driving on the right in 1970, even though many of its cars are right-hand drive.
traps.Vanuatu: It drives on the right, despite its British and French past.

title: Half past
q: Countries with a time zone offset by 30 or 45 minutes from UTC
rule: Standard time ending in :30 or :45. Any inhabited part of a country counts, so overseas territories do too.
fact: France qualifies through the Marquesas Islands in French Polynesia, which keep UTC-9:30. New Zealand qualifies through the Chatham Islands, at UTC+12:45.

traps.Pakistan: It runs on UTC+5, a whole hour.
traps.Bangladesh: It runs on UTC+6, a whole hour.
traps.Bhutan: It runs on UTC+6, a whole hour.
traps.Venezuela: It kept a half-hour offset until 2016, then moved to whole-hour UTC-4.
traps.North Korea: Its half-hour Pyongyang Time lasted from 2015 to 2018, then it went back to UTC+9.

title: Short and sweet
q: Countries with exactly four letters in their name
rule: UN member states, using the usual short English name.
fact: Four letters is as short as a country name gets: no UN member state has a three-letter English name.

traps.Guam: It has four letters, but it's a US territory, not a country.
traps.Niue: It has four letters, but it isn't a UN member state.

title: Fit in Wales
q: Countries smaller than Wales (about 20,800 km²)
rule: UN members plus the Pope's own state, by total area. Wales is 20,779 km². Israel is too close to call, so it's out.
fact: Slovenia, Kuwait, Fiji and Eswatini are all smaller than Wales, which could hold the Vatican more than 40,000 times.

traps.El Salvador: At about 21,000 km² it is just bigger than Wales.
traps.Belize: At about 23,000 km² it is bigger than Wales.
traps.Djibouti: At about 23,200 km² it is bigger than Wales.
traps.Rwanda: At about 26,300 km² it is bigger than Wales.
traps.Lesotho: At about 30,400 km² it is bigger than Wales.

title: Missing vowels
q: African countries with no E, I or Y in their name
rule: Checked against the usual English name.
fact: South Sudan became independent in 2011, making it the newest country in Africa.

traps.Egypt: It has a Y, so it misses.
traps.Tanzania: It has an I in it.
traps.Kenya: It has an E and a Y.

title: Shore thing
q: Countries with a coastline on the Baltic Sea
rule: A coast on a detached exclave of a country counts.
fact: Russia's Baltic coast sits in Kaliningrad, an exclave cut off from the rest of Russia by Lithuania and Poland.

traps.Norway: Its coast faces the North Sea and the Norwegian Sea, not the Baltic.
traps.Ukraine: Its coast is on the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.

title: Most neighbours
q: Countries that share a land border with Brazil
rule: The border of an overseas region of a European country counts.
fact: Brazil borders every South American country except Chile and Ecuador.

traps.Chile: It has long Andean borders with Peru, Bolivia and Argentina, but none with Brazil.
traps.Ecuador: Peru and Colombia sit between Ecuador and Brazil.
traps.Portugal: Portuguese is Brazil's language, but Portugal is in Europe, not a neighbour.

title: Named after someone
q: National capital cities named after a real person
rule: The name must honour one specific real person, such as a monarch, politician or explorer. Saints and names that just mean 'king's town' don't count.
fact: Malabo, Equatorial Guinea's capital, was called Santa Isabel until 1973, when it was renamed after Malabo Lopelo Melaka, the last king of the Bubi people.

traps.Bridgetown: It takes its name from a bridge, not a person.
traps.Ottawa: It's named after the Odawa people.
traps.Freetown: It was founded for freed people, and isn't named after one person.
traps.Kingston: It means 'king's town' and honours no single person.
traps.Ulaanbaatar: Means 'red hero', a title rather than a person's name.

title: Island hopping
q: Sovereign Caribbean countries made up of islands
rule: Sovereign states only, so Puerto Rico (a US territory) doesn't count.
fact: Haiti and the Dominican Republic share the island of Hispaniola.

traps.Puerto Rico: It's a US territory, not a sovereign state.
traps.Belize: It's on the Central American mainland.
traps.Guyana: It's on the South American mainland.

title: In name only
q: Countries whose official name includes the word Democratic
rule: Use the full official name in force today. Former names like East Germany's don't count.
fact: Ethiopia adopted its current name, the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, in 1995.

traps.Republic of the Congo: Its official name has no Democratic in it.
traps.Yemen: It's officially the Republic of Yemen, with no Democratic in its name.
traps.Germany: East Germany was the German Democratic Republic, but that state no longer exists.

title: Crowded frontier
q: Countries that share a land border with the DRC
rule: A border on a lake still counts as a land border.
fact: The DRC has nine land neighbours, the most of any African country.

traps.Sudan: It borders South Sudan, but not the DRC.
traps.Kenya: Uganda and Tanzania sit between Kenya and the DRC.
traps.Malawi: Tanzania and Zambia sit between Malawi and the DRC.

title: Thin air
q: Mountains over 8,000 metres high
rule: The peak must be over 8,000 m. Its other common name also counts.
fact: Shishapangma is the only 8,000 m peak lying entirely inside China's borders, in Tibet.

traps.Mount Kilimanjaro: It's about 5,900 m, well short of 8,000.
traps.Aconcagua: South America's highest, at about 6,960 m.

title: Royal flush
q: European countries with a monarch as head of state
rule: Andorra's co-princes and Vatican City's elected pope don't count.
fact: Liechtenstein is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world, with Uzbekistan.

traps.Italy: It had a king until a 1946 referendum made it a republic.
traps.Germany: It has been a republic since 1918 and has no monarch.
traps.Portugal: It has been a republic since 1910.

title: Ending up
q: European countries whose name ends in IA
rule: Only countries usually placed in Europe count. Countries of the Caucasus are excluded.
fact: North Macedonia adopted its current name in 2019, after a deal with Greece over the old one.

traps.Italy: It ends in Y, not IA.
traps.Armenia: It ends in IA but is usually placed in the Caucasus, not Europe.
traps.Georgia: It ends in IA but is usually placed in the Caucasus, not Europe.

title: Hide and seek
q: Countries whose name hides the full name of another country
rule: The hidden name must be a usual short name, spelled letter for letter inside the name.
fact: Somalia hides the name of Mali, a landlocked country in West Africa.

traps.Malaysia: Its name contains no other country's name.
traps.Tanzania: Its name contains no other country's name.
traps.Pakistan: Its name contains no other country's name.

title: Fenced in
q: Countries that share a land border with Iran
rule: A border through a neighbour's exclave counts. A maritime boundary doesn't.
fact: Iran has seven land neighbours, and it also shares the Caspian Sea with Russia.

traps.Russia: Iran and Russia share the Caspian Sea, not a land border.
traps.Saudi Arabia: The Persian Gulf separates it from Iran.

title: Parish pump
q: Parishes of Jersey, the Channel Island
rule: Only the twelve parishes of Jersey count, not the Guernsey or Alderney parishes.
fact: Jersey's capital, St Helier, is named after a 6th-century hermit who was killed by pirates.

traps.St Peter Port: That's Guernsey's capital, not a Jersey parish.
traps.Alderney: It's a Guernsey island, not a Jersey parish.
traps.Guernsey: It's an island, not a parish of Jersey.

title: Crowded shores
q: Lakes shared by three or more countries
rule: Enclosed inland waters that are legally lakes count, even when they're called seas.
fact: Lake Victoria is Africa's largest lake by area, and three countries share its shores.

traps.Lake Titicaca: Only Peru and Bolivia share it.
traps.Lake Geneva: Only France and Switzerland share it.
traps.Lake Superior: Only Canada and the United States share it.

title: Riverside
q: London boroughs that touch the River Thames
rule: A local authority counts if any part of its boundary meets the river.
fact: Richmond Park, in Richmond upon Thames, is one of London's Royal Parks and has free-roaming deer.

traps.Croydon: A south London borough that's nowhere near the river.
traps.Barnet: A north London borough with no Thames frontage.

title: Open endings
q: Oceania countries whose name ends in A or U
rule: Sovereign states only, judged on the usual English name.
fact: Nauru, about 21 square kilometres, is the third-smallest country in the world, after the Vatican and Monaco.

traps.Fiji: It ends in I, so it misses.
traps.Kiribati: It ends in I, so it misses.

title: Corner flags
q: Pacific countries and territories with a Union Jack on their flag
rule: The whole flag of the UK doesn't count. Sub-national states within federations don't count.
fact: Fiji's flag has kept the Union Jack in its corner since independence in 1970.

traps.United Kingdom: Its whole flag is the Union Jack, so it isn't a flag with one in the corner.
traps.Hawaii: It's a US state, so it doesn't count.
traps.Canada: Its flag is a red maple leaf, with no Union Jack.
traps.Japan: Its flag is a red disc on white.

title: Blueprint
q: National capitals that were built specially to be capitals
rule: Built or laid out from scratch to be the national capital, including those still being finished. Cities that were simply chosen as capital don't count.
fact: Brasília was built from scratch in about four years and opened as Brazil's capital in 1960.

traps.Ottawa: It was an existing town that Queen Victoria chose, not a city built for the job.
traps.Chandigarh: It was planned, but it's a state capital, not a national one.

title: Saudade
q: Sovereign countries where Portuguese is an official language
rule: Portuguese must be an official language nationally, so Macau doesn't count.
fact: Brazil has more Portuguese speakers than all the other Portuguese-speaking countries put together.

traps.Spain: Spanish is its official language, not Portuguese.
traps.Macau: Portuguese is official there, but Macau isn't a sovereign state.
traps.Goa: It was Portuguese once, but it's an Indian state where Portuguese isn't official.

title: Red alert
q: Countries with a coastline on the Red Sea
rule: A coast on a gulf that branches off the sea counts.
fact: The Suez Canal links the Red Sea to the Mediterranean, and it opened in 1869.

traps.Somalia: Its coast is on the Indian Ocean and the Gulf of Aden.
traps.Oman: Its coast is on the Arabian Sea and the Gulf of Oman.
traps.Iran: Its coast is on the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

title: Continental tops
q: The highest peak on each continent, by the Seven Summits list
rule: For Oceania, either of the two accepted peaks counts.
fact: Denali was officially renamed from Mount McKinley in 2015, though the older name is still widely used.

traps.Mont Blanc: Highest in the Alps, but Europe's top peak is Mount Elbrus.
traps.Mount Fuji: Japan's highest, but not the highest in Asia.

title: Dog days
q: The seven main islands of a Spanish archipelago off Africa
rule: Only the seven large inhabited islands count. Small islets don't.
fact: The archipelago's name is traditionally linked to dogs, from the Latin word canis.

traps.La Graciosa: A small inhabited islet, not one of the seven main islands.
traps.Madeira: A Portuguese archipelago, not a Spanish one.

title: Two oceans
q: Countries with mainland coasts on both the Pacific and the Atlantic
rule: The Caribbean counts as part of the Atlantic. Islands alone don't count.
fact: The Panama Canal, opened in 1914, cuts across Panama to link the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

traps.Peru: Its coast faces only the Pacific.
traps.Brazil: Its coast faces only the Atlantic.
traps.Ecuador: Its only mainland coast faces the Pacific.

title: Dry land
q: Welsh principal areas with no coastline
rule: Any shore counts, so Monmouthshire and Flintshire (estuary shores) don't qualify.
fact: Powys is the largest Welsh principal area by area, and it has no coastline at all.

traps.Monmouthshire: It has a shore on the Severn estuary, so it has a coastline.
traps.Flintshire: It has a shore on the Dee estuary, so it has a coastline.
traps.Pembrokeshire: It has a long Atlantic coastline.
